text: I’ll represent the planar fluid region as the union of a 6 mm straight channel and four 6 mm-wide asymmetric Bézier arches. Each arch branches from and rejoins the main passage, leaving a teardrop-shaped island between the arch and straight path. Since the request does not specify loop proportions, I’ll initially assume 22 mm branch-to-rejoin spacing, 12 mm loop rise, and 1 mm extrusion thickness for a one-cell 2D OpenFOAM mesh. This first pass creates and displays only a coarse planar mesh so the topology can be checked before extrusion and patching.

The first union produced many conformal sub-surfaces rather than one clean fluid face, and the plotting extraction also used the Gmsh return tuple incorrectly. I’m discarding that failed construction and checking whether the available planar-geometry library can create a single, clean buffered path before handing it to Gmsh.
I’ll reissue the dependency check as a self-contained script cell so the final build remains replayable.

I’ll replace the overlapping boolean pieces with one explicit planar boundary: the outer loop follows the main-channel walls and the outer side of each arch, while four inner loops bound the teardrop islands. This also creates the inlet, outlet, and wall curves semantically at construction time rather than recovering them by bounding-box position.

The explicit shape is sound, but Gmsh requires adjacent curves to share the same point tags—not merely coincident coordinates. I’ll rebuild the same topology while explicitly reusing endpoint tags, then display the coarse planar mesh.

The coarse view confirms one connected straight passage, four distinct bypasses, and four enclosed teardrop islands. I’ll now extrude this exact planar face by the assumed 1 mm thickness with one cell through the plane. Lateral faces will be classified by their topological connection to the already named inlet/outlet curves; all remaining lateral faces are walls, and the two planar faces are grouped as `frontAndBack`.

The extrusion produced 1,141 one-layer prism cells with the intended five patch groups. I’ll convert the Gmsh mesh to OpenFOAM, add only the minimal case metadata needed by mesh utilities, and inspect the converted boundary file before changing any mesh patch types.

Conversion is consistent: 1,141 prisms, 2,282 front/back triangles, 215 wall faces, and four faces on each end. The “undefined faces” message is Gmsh-to-OpenFOAM’s intermediate handling of internal faces; no `defaultFaces` patch remains. I’ll now set only mesh patch types (`empty` for the planar pair and `wall` for walls) and run the binding mesh-quality check.

`checkMesh` reached the case but OpenFOAM 2512 requires `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` files even for this mesh-only invocation. I’ll add empty valid dictionaries and rerun the same full topology/geometry check.
This release parses the standard scheme subdictionaries during geometric checks. I’ll supply minimal defaults (still no solver setup or boundary conditions) and rerun.

The full check passes. Before finishing, I’ll export the already named OpenFOAM boundary patches as separate STL files for downstream inspection; first I’ll confirm the installed `surfaceMeshExtract` command syntax.
I’ll export exactly four non-overlapping patch STLs—`inlet`, `outlet`, `walls`, and `frontAndBack`. Their union is the closed fluid-volume boundary; no duplicate combined STL will be added.

`surfaceMeshExtract` skipped the faces on the `empty` patch, yielding an empty planar STL. I’ll temporarily present that mesh patch to the extractor as a generic patch, overwrite only `frontAndBack.stl`, and immediately restore its final `empty` type. This does not change mesh geometry or solver boundary data.

I’ll perform a final geometric audit against the request and the stated assumptions, then verify that the union of all four patch groups forms a closed triangulated surface. Width is measured between the two constructed offset curves, while length and thickness are measured from the final extruded volume bounds.

The final geometry is a 120 mm planar Tesla-valve fluid domain with a measured 6.000 mm channel width and four teardrop bypass loops. The coarse one-layer mesh contains 1,141 triangular prisms; `checkMesh -allGeometry -allTopology` reports **Mesh OK**, and the combined patch surface is closed and connected.

Assumptions chosen because they were not specified: 22 mm branch-to-rejoin span, asymmetric Bézier loop shape with 9 mm measured centerline rise (about 12 mm outer height above the main centerline), and 1 mm extrusion solely to realize a 2D OpenFOAM mesh. Patches are `inlet`, `outlet`, `walls`, and `frontAndBack` (`empty`). No flow boundary conditions were created and no solve was run.
